docs.title: PurpleAI
docs.text: PurpleAI combines an IDUN-backed attacker with asynchronous execution subagents, an HTTP defender that classifies SQL injection and XSS, deliberately vulnerable web applications, and centralized Vector logging.

docs.title: Repository components
docs.text:
• src/Attacker/: autonomous Boss, execution subagents, tools, and event logging.
  • src/defender/defender-agent/: Flask reverse proxy and request classifiers.
  • src/defender/vulnerable-app/: VulnShop Flask/SQLite application.
  • src/purpleai_logging.py: shared JSON event logger.
  • deploy/vector/: sender and gamehost receiver configurations and host setup guide.
  • src/gamehost/traffic/: k6 scenarios targeting VulnShop routes.
  • src/gamehost/dashboard/: Streamlit dashboard reading Vector archives.

The component READMEs contain startup commands and configuration.

docs.title: Event logging
docs.text:
Applications print JSON events and append them to local files. Vector on RedAI and BlueAI tails those files and forwards them to gamehost Vector on TCP 6000. Gamehost writes daily JSONL archives under /var/log/purpleai/collected/.

The event format documents the shared envelope and current actions. File paths, service setup, and retention behavior are covered by deploy/vector/README.md in the repository.

docs.title: PurpleAI event log format
docs.text: The attacker and defender use src/purpleai_logging.py to print each event and append it to a local JSON Lines file. Host Vector agents tail these files and forward events to gamehost Vector, which writes daily JSONL archives. This page describes the shared event format.

docs.title: Envelope
docs.text:
Every event is a single JSON object with these fields:

Field Type Required Description schema_version integer yes Always 1. Bump only for breaking changes. event_id string yes UUID v4 string, unique per event. run_id string yes UUID v4 string shared by all events from one agent run. timestamp string yes ISO 8601 in UTC (offset must be +00:00/Z), e.g. 2026-10-01T12:34:56.789+00:00. source string yes Name of the sending agent, e.g. attacker-agent. One word, hyphens allowed. actor string yes Who acted, e.g. attacker, defender, analyst. action string yes What happened, e.g. task_start, tool_call. tool string no Tool used, e.g. nmap. Omit when not applicable. target string no Target of the action, e.g. 192.168.50.10:8080. Omit when not applicable. status string no Outcome, e.g. started, success, failure. Omit while unknown.

Rules:

  • Omit optional fields rather than sending null or empty strings.
  • Source-specific fields may be added alongside the envelope. Defender events include request_id, method, path, decision, http_status, and error_type when applicable.
  • The shared logger supplies the envelope; agent fields cannot override it.
  • Vector can retry delivery. Consumers should use event_id to identify duplicates in the archive.

docs.title: Standard actions
docs.text:
Use this vocabulary so logs are comparable across agents:

Action Meaning Typical fields task_start Agent run begins status: started task_end Agent run ends status: stopped, error, or cancelled for the autonomous attacker tool_call Agent invokes a tool tool, target tool_result Tool returned output tool, target, status request_decision Defender allows or blocks a request request_id, decision, status request_result Upstream response or forwarding error request_id, http_status or error_type, status iteration_start, iteration_end One autonomous Boss turn iteration, operation_id, duration_ms on end agent_tool_call, agent_tool_result Boss framework tool/delegation activity tool, tool_call_id, task_id when supplied subagent_status Remote execution task state task_id, subagent, remote_run_id, status

The attacker runs until interrupted: task_end normally has status: stopped. Unexpected exceptions use error; cancellation propagated out of a span uses cancelled. Actual tool calls/results share a tool_call_id and carry task_id when run by the execution server. The server's task ID connects these events to the Boss's subagent_status events across process-local run_id values. Tool results add duration_ms, exit_code when available, and error_type for exceptions. Tool completed and subagent success describe execution, not confirmed exploitation. The dashboard counts tool calls/errors and defender block decisions, not inferred attack success.

New actions are fine when the existing ones do not fit; keep them snake_case and descriptive.

docs.title: File output and delivery
docs.text:
Both agents use log_event("action", status="...", **fields). Their small logging adapters configure the source, actor, and default file path; the shared logger handles serialization, IDs, UTC timestamps, and file output through Python's WatchedFileHandler.

Host Vector reads the JSONL file, parses the JSON, and preserves the event fields while adding the sending host, file, and source_type. The gamehost receives Vector transport on TCP 6000 and archives events at /var/log/purpleai/collected/events-%Y-%m-%d.jsonl.

The Vector pipeline parses JSON objects; it does not validate every envelope field. The shared logger supplies the standard envelope. File errors are reported without stopping the agent. Host Vector handles delivery retries and buffering separately from application execution.

See deploy/vector/README.md in the repository for host configuration, permissions, buffering, and retention.

docs.title: Correlating a lab run
docs.text:
Set the same optional PURPLEAI_ENGAGEMENT_ID on the RedAI Boss, RedAI execution server, and in the gamehost k6 environment. Use a short identifier such as lab-run-1 (letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens). RedAI attaches it to its events. BlueAI records it from valid traffic tags.

  • sqlmap and XSSer send their execution's tool_call_id as X-PurpleAI-Traffic, followed by a space and the optional engagement ID. BlueAI records it on decisions and results with traffic_source: redai. k6 sends k6 in that header and the optional ID in X-PurpleAI-Engagement. BlueAI records traffic_source: k6. Missing or invalid tags leave the source unknown. These are self-reported labels for controlled lab traffic.
  • BlueAI generates X-PurpleAI-Request-ID on forwarding. VulnShop's objective_served event carries that ID when it renders the admin page. This records page access, including legitimate admin access.
  • BlueAI's duration_ms measures classification on decisions and forwarding on results. A detection or classifier error includes classifier, the classifier that stopped evaluation.
  • A tool-side flag_captured includes the execution and task IDs when available. It describes a string seen in tool output. Boss observations can repeat the same flag, so these events should not be counted as unique objective completions.
